{{< include _elements-kit.qmd >}}

**Metre** is how the steady beat (the **pulse**) is grouped. The strong beat comes round regularly: every 2, 3 or 4 beats.
Each group is a [measure]{.nn}.

## 1. Time signatures

A time signature is written at the start of the music, and again wherever it changes.

- The **top number** says how many beats in each [measure]{.nn} (in simple time).
- The **bottom number** says what kind of note gets the beat: 4 = [quarter note]{.nn}, 2 = [half note]{.nn}, 8 =
  [eighth note]{.nn}.

**C** is short for 4/4, called **common time**. **C with a line through it** is 2/2, **cut time** (*alla breve*).

## 2. Simple time

In **simple time** each beat splits into **two** equal halves.

| Time signature | Beats in a [measure]{.nn} | Name | Often heard in |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2/4 | 2 [quarter notes]{.nn} | simple duple | marches, polkas |
| 3/4 | 3 [quarter notes]{.nn} | simple triple | waltzes, minuets |
| 4/4 | 4 [quarter notes]{.nn} | simple quadruple | most pop, rock and jazz |

Listen for where the strong beat (the accent) falls:

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="112" data-style="pop"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:2/4: ONE two, ONE two
M:2/4
L:1/8
K:C
"C"!>!c2 G2|"G"!>!B2 G2|"C"!>!c2 e2|"G"!>!d4|"C"!>!c2 G2|"G"!>!B2 D2|"C"!>!C4|z4|]
</script></div>

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="132" data-style="waltz"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:3/4: ONE two three
M:3/4
L:1/4
K:G
"G"!>!G B d|"D"!>!A F D|"G"!>!G B d|"C"!>!c2 B|"D"!>!A F A|"G"!>!G3|]
</script></div>

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100" data-style="rock"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:4/4: ONE two three four
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:A
"A"!>!A c e c|"D"!>!d f a f|"E"!>!e B G B|"A"!>!A4|]
</script></div>

## 3. Compound time

In **compound time** each beat is a dotted note and splits into **three**. The top number counts the
[eighth notes]{.nn}, not the beats: divide it by three to get the beats.

| Time signature | [Eighth notes]{.nn} | Beats (dotted [quarter notes]{.nn}) | Name |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6/8 | 6 | 2 | compound duple |
| 9/8 | 9 | 3 | compound triple |
| 12/8 | 12 | 4 | compound quadruple |

The same tune in 2/4 and in 6/8. Both have two beats in a [measure]{.nn}; listen to how each beat divides:

::: {.ax-pair}
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:2/4: each beat in two
M:2/4
L:1/16
K:D
!>!A2B2 !>!A2F2|!>!E2F2 !>!E2C2|!>!A2B2 !>!A2F2|!>!E4 !>!D4|]
</script></div>

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:6/8: each beat in three
M:6/8
L:1/8
Q:3/8=100
K:D
!>!ABA !>!F2D|!>!EFE !>!C3|!>!ABA !>!F2A|!>!E3 !>!D3|]
</script></div>
:::

12/8 is the slow, rolling feel of many blues and soul ballads: four beats, each in three.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="60" data-style="ballad"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:12/8
M:12/8
L:1/8
Q:3/8=60
K:C
"C"E2G c2G E2G c2G|"F"F2A c2A "G"G2B d3|"C"c12|]
</script></div>

## 4. Hearing the metre

1. Tap the pulse with your foot.
2. Listen for the strongest beat, often where the bass note or the chord changes, and count from it: **1** 2 3 **1** 2 3...
3. Listen *between* the beats. If the beat naturally splits in two, it is simple time; if it splits in three (a
   lilting, "jig" feel), it is compound.

A march is usually in two (left, right, left, right). A waltz is a dance in three.

## 5. Regular and irregular metres

A **regular** metre divides into equal groups of two or three beats (2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8, 9/8, 12/8). An **irregular**
metre can't: 5/4 is counted 3 + 2 (or 2 + 3), 7/8 as 2 + 2 + 3. Some music also **changes** metre as it goes, which is a
good way to make contrast in your own pieces.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="160"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:5/4, grouped 3 + 2
M:5/4
L:1/4
K:Em
"Em"!>!E G B !>!A G|"Am"!>!A c e !>!d c|"B7"!>!B ^d f !>!e d|"Em"!>!E3 !>!E2|]
</script></div>

## 6. Recordings to try

Find these and count along. Metres from the school handout, not yet checked against the scores:

| Metre | Piece |
|---|---|
| 2/4 | *Slaidburn* (William Rimmer), a brass band march |
| 3/4 | Shostakovich, *Waltz No. 2* |
| 4/4 | *All That Jazz* from the musical *Chicago* |
| 5/4 | Dave Brubeck Quartet, *Take Five* |
| 7/4 | Pink Floyd, *Money* (the opening bass riff) |
| 6/8 | Queen, *We Are the Champions* |
| 12/8 | Michael Jackson, *The Way You Make Me Feel* (count 1-&-a 2-&-a 3-&-a 4-&-a) |

## 7. Writing your own

Every [measure]{.nn} must add up to the time signature: check each one before you hand it in. Changing metre for one section is a simple way to make contrast.
